title: Catalog API contract decision for paginated item retrieval
purpose: Document the two competing Catalog API pagination drafts, the resulting unresolved contract decision, and the proposed handoff stories so a human can choose an authoritative contract before implementation.

scope.text: The feature under consideration is retrieval of catalog items from GET /v1/items.

Two draft response shapes are in evidence: a draft returning a JSON object with an items array and next_cursor string, and a draft returning a top-level JSON array with page and page_size query parameters.
Neither draft is approved; the authoritative contract has not been selected.

requirements.text: GET /v1/items returns a JSON object with an items array and next_cursor string.
UI must support moving to the next page.
GET /v1/items returns a top-level JSON array and uses page and page_size query parameters.

stories.text: If a human selects draft A as the authoritative contract, a UI consumer can request GET /v1/items and move to the next page using the returned cursor.
acceptance_criteria: Given a human has selected draft A as the authoritative contract, when GET /v1/items is called, then the response body is a JSON object containing an items array.
Given a human has selected draft A as the authoritative contract, when GET /v1/items is called, then the response body contains a next_cursor string.

Given a human has selected draft A as the authoritative contract, when the UI has a non-empty next cursor and the user moves to the next page, then the UI requests the page identified by that cursor and displays the returned items.

stories.text: If a human selects draft B as the authoritative contract, an API consumer can request GET /v1/items with page and page_size and receive the requested page of catalog items.
acceptance_criteria: Given a human has selected draft B as the authoritative contract, when GET /v1/items is called, then the response body is a top-level JSON array.

Given a human has selected draft B as the authoritative contract, when GET /v1/items is called with page and page_size query parameters, then the returned items correspond to the requested page at the requested page size.

edge_cases.text: Draft A returns a next_cursor string while draft B returns a top-level JSON array; a client cannot satisfy both response shapes simultaneously.
A next page may or may not exist; whether an end-of-results condition is represented, and how, is not supplied.
Whether a first page or default page size is required for draft B, and what a caller sends to obtain it, is not supplied.

dependencies.text: Implementation depends on a human selecting which draft is the authoritative contract.

risks.text: Selecting draft A would fail the draft B response shape and query parameter request; selecting draft B would fail the draft A response shape and next-page cursor request.
Implementing against an unselected draft risks rework once the authoritative contract is chosen.

success_metrics.text: Verification could check that, for the selected contract, a request to GET /v1/items returns the selected draft's response shape and that following the selected draft's pagination mechanism yields the next set of catalog items.

open_questions: Which draft is the authoritative contract for GET /v1/items: draft A or draft B?
Who has authority to select the authoritative contract?
If draft A is selected, does the draft B obligation to accept page and page_size query parameters still apply?
If draft B is selected, does the draft A obligation for the UI to support moving to the next page still apply?
If draft A is selected, how does a client supply the value of next_cursor from a previous response in the next request?
If draft A is selected, how is the end of results indicated when no next page exists, and what does next_cursor contain in that case?
If draft A is selected, is the cursor an opaque value, and does the contract define its validity window or ordering basis?

If draft B is selected, are page and page_size required or optional, what are their defaults, what is the numbering basis of page (for example zero- or one-based), and how does a caller detect that no further pages exist?
